name: FillTox facial

card.summary: A single-visit facial treatment that combines dermal filler for lost volume with botulinum toxin for movement lines, aiming for a smoother, fuller, more youthful face.
card.note: Injectable procedures performed by clinicians; filler and toxin each carry their own complications.

quick.overview:
FillTox is a nickname for a facial session in which a clinician uses both dermal filler and botulinum toxin (such as Botox). Toxin relaxes the muscles behind expression lines, mostly in the upper face, and filler restores volume or contour in areas such as the cheeks, lips and jawline.

Providers call the combination a liquid facelift. Dermatologist Marina Landau says ageing involves skin, fat, muscle and bone, and that combining treatments addresses more than one cause [1]. Published same-session studies are limited.
quick.how: A licensed injector treats movement lines with toxin and volume loss with filler, sometimes in one sitting. Toxin smoothing is usually visible within days and lasts two to four months, sometimes longer; most wrinkle fillers last about six months [2][3].
quick.risks: Toxin can spread to unintended muscles, causing weakness, drooping or double vision in reported cases [2]. Filler complications range from bruising and lumps to rare vascular events including permanent vision loss [3]. Landau reports no added complications from using both in different areas, with a slight potential for added toxin spread when both go in the same spot at once [1].

lead: FillTox is a colloquial term for a facial treatment combining a dermal filler with a botulinum toxin neuromodulator in the same session. Botulinum toxin blocks nerve signals so the muscles under wrinkles relax, and works best in the upper third of the face [2]. Fillers, most commonly hyaluronic acid, smooth folds, restore volume lost with age, and enhance lips, cheeks and jawline [3].

Clinics describe the combination as a liquid facelift that handles both the movement and the volume components of ageing [4]. Landau notes that muscle dominates ageing in the upper face while volume loss dominates in the midface, and that treating the same spot with both can give a more durable correction for deep glabellar lines or downturned mouth corners [1].

A published case series reported calcium hydroxylapatite filler, hyaluronic acid filler and incobotulinumtoxinA in one visit and described the agents as synergistic, while noting same-day trials were scarce [4].

chain: Toxin relaxes muscles behind expression lines
angle.text: The toxin softens lines caused by muscle movement and the filler replaces lost volume, together giving a smoother and fuller face in one visit. Results are temporary and are repeated by those who want to maintain them.

infobox: About 6 months for many wrinkle fillers [3]
Botox Cosmetic FDA-approved for frown lines 2002 [2]; fillers regulated as devices [3]

paras: Cosmetic use of botulinum toxin for wrinkles was first reported in 1989 by plastic surgeon Richard Clark, studied for glabellar lines by the Carruthers in 1992, and FDA-approved for frown lines in 2002 [2]. Fillers are mostly hydrogels; hyaluronic acid is the most common [3].
Toxin effects are usually visible three to five days after injection and peak about a week later [2].

Landau says using filler and toxin in different areas, or in the same area at different sittings, has not been reported to add complications; injecting both into the same spot at once may slightly raise toxin diffusion [1]. She raises the question of whether to space or combine treatments and which to inject first, without prescribing an order [1]. A physician answer on RealSelf, anecdotal rather than a guideline, suggests toxin first when both go in the glabella [5].

Toxin side effects include headaches, allergic reactions, spread to unintended muscles and, rarely, temporary double vision [2]. Filler commonly causes bruising, redness, pain and itching; infections, lumps, and rare embolic events including permanent blindness have been reported [3].

Published same-session evidence is limited to case series and clinician reports, which describe combined treatment in a single visit as feasible [4][1]. Individual toxin and filler products have their own clinical literature [2][3].

timeline.event: Richard Clark reports toxin used for wrinkles [2].
Carruthers studies toxin for glabellar lines [2].
FDA approves Botox Cosmetic for moderate-to-severe frown lines [2].
